description: We are Iridium, a diverse team of curious minds united by our love for learning, space technology and creative thinking. With different talents, perspectives and ideas, we enjoy exploring the unknown, connecting seemingly unrelated dots and turning bold thoughts into innovative possibilities. We believe that great ideas grow through collaboration and curiosity. For us, the world is a place of infinite possibilities, and we are here to imagine, explore and create beyond what we know today.
summary:
ATTENTION ALL RANGERS!!  In a few minutes, you’ll be headed for your next mission. Astronauts on the moon have uncovered ground-breaking research that may help humans inhabit mars. But they are facing some challenges and you must bring them bring them back to earth safely.

In Astro MarLuna, you will encounter day to day challenges in food production, Temperature controls, Power management, medical emergencies, Radiation shielding and life support and make consequential decisions that  demonstrate why balancing resources is essential for survival.  

Astro MarLuna uses real NASA data and concepts in   Selenology(the study of the moon) and Areology(the study of mars) to help kids experience life in space through a playful, high-space adventure. With it’s unique integration of APOD KPI and DONKI KPI we simulate real space conditions helping  kids bridge the gap between imagination and scientific concepts. 

The downloadable offline feature makes the game accessible to children in communities with limited internet connectivity, ensuring access to quality STEM education is not limited by geography or digital infrastructure.

Our aim to empower kids through digital education is to make space science accessible and ignite the curiosity and critical thinking needed to solve humanity's challenges beyond Earth within the next generation.
details:
Project Solution
Space can be a very exciting classroom for kids. Yet, many  miss out on the opportunity to explore due to how we teach about it.
Astro MarLuna is a game where kids run a lunar outpost, the Kennedy Post, during a solar storm. Their mission is to save stranded astronauts by helping them to manage storms and resources simulating what  scientists might encounter in real life while learning along the way.

How Does Our Solution Work?

Astro MarLuna immerses players in a story-driven lunar rescue mission. Players are recruited as space rangers and sent on a rescue mission to Kennedy Post, a lunar outpost facing an approaching solar storm. Upon arrival, they discover that the astronauts are struggling to keep the settlement operational. With time running out, players must    investigate its failing systems and help the crew overcome a series of survival challenges.


Along the way, players encounter   missions inspired by the 7 adversities  of space exploration:

1. Radiation Shielding: Help protect astronauts from harmful solar radiation by identifying suitable shielding methods and securing a safe shelter.

2. Power Management: Manage the outpost's limited energy supply by prioritising essential systems and preventing power shortages.

3. Life Support: Restore the systems responsible for maintaining breathable air and safe living conditions inside the habitat.

4. Food Production: Help sustain the crew by managing a lunar greenhouse, growing crops and making the most of limited resources.

5. Water and Waste Management: Restore water recycling systems, conserve available supplies and minimise waste.

6. Temperature Control: Regulate the habitat's heating and cooling systems to protect astronauts from extreme lunar temperatures.

7. Medical Emergencies: Respond to astronauts experiencing health complications by identifying symptoms and selecting appropriate first-aid supplies.

Benefits of the Game:        

  • Critical thinking: Encourages players to analyse situations and make informed decisions.
  • Resource management: Teaches the importance of conserving limited resources.
  • Digital inclusion: Downloadable offline gameplay makes learning possible without continuous internet access.
  • Scientific curiosity: Introduces children to real NASA research and the challenges of human space exploration.  
  • STEM awareness: Introduces children to astronomy, space science, engineering and scientific problem-solving.
  • Experiential learning: Turns abstract space-science concepts into interactive experiences.

Our goal

Our goal is to make space science accessible, engaging and experiential for children, regardless of their geographical location or access to internet connectivity.

We hope to develop early STEM skills and encourage the next generation of scientists  and explorers.

 

Tools and Technologies Used

Coding Languages: 1. React
2. TypeScript (TSX)
3. Vite Development
4. Three.js 3D
5. React Three Fiber
6. Tailwind CSS
7. JavaScript


                               

Character Design: https://arena.ai
                                

Voice/sound: https://suno.com/
                             

Creative Aspects and Things considered:

1.We intentionally used certain names and characters inspired by historical NASA events (ie. a. from Neil Armstrong as Neilstrom,
                   b. Edwin “Buzz” Aldwin as Buzztronaut  
                   c. Michael Collins as Micollins
                   d. Mae Jemison as Maestrix
                   e. Sally Ride as Sally Strike
                   f. Christiana Koch as Kochsmos
                   g. Kennedy Space Center in Florida as Kennedy Outpost on the moon )

2.We added a catchy high tempo theme song to create a sense of community among kids.

3.We provided a download feature so players can learn through the game even in areas with limited or unreliable internet access.

4.Our project supports the following UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being: Raises awareness of astronaut health, radiation protection and medical care throughout questions in the challenge.

SDG 4 – Quality Education: Makes STEM education engaging and accessible through interactive missions and problem-solving.

SDG 5 – Gender Equality: Encourages children of all genders to explore STEM and challenge gender stereotypes in science and technology.

SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production: Teaches responsible resource management through challenges involving limited food, water, energy, and materials.

SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals: Utilizing NASA’s open scientific resources with other skills and resources to make space research and knowledge accessible for learning.
